topic: The Windmill Problem: A Dance of Geometry and Combinatorics
target_audience: High school students interested in competition math (IMO level concepts) and curious problem solvers.

sections.title: Introduction: The Infinite Spinner
lecture_lines: Imagine points like stars scattered across a map.
We place a rotating line through one central point.
As the line spins, it strikes another point.
The pivot point then jumps to this new star.
Can this simple dance visit every single point?
animations: Fade in 5 points at random positions (color: #FFFFFF). self.wait(1.5).
Create a long line through a central point (color: #FFD700). self.wait(2.0).
Rotate the line clockwise; when it hits another point, flash that point (color: #00FF00). self.wait(1.5).
Shift the line's pivot point to the hit point and continue rotation. self.wait(2.0).
Highlight all points with a pulsing glow to indicate potential visitation (color: #FF4500). self.wait(2.0).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game
lecture_lines: No three points lie on a single straight line.
The line rotates until it strikes exactly one point.
The pivot immediately shifts to this new point.
animations: Show 3 points in a triangle (#FFFFFF); draw a line through two and show a red 'X' to indicate invalidity. self.wait(2.0).
Show a line rotating clockwise around a single pivot point (color: #FFD700). self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line until it strikes exactly one new point; highlight the intersection (color: #00FF00). self.wait(2.0).

sections.title: The Mechanism of the Pivot
lecture_lines: Watch the line sweep across the plane like radar.
Upon impact, the center of rotation instantly changes.
The clockwise motion remains constant throughout the dance.
animations: Animate the line sweeping clockwise like a radar beam, leaving a faint trail (color: #FFD700). self.wait(1.5).
When the line hits a point, shift the pivot point instantly and flash the new pivot (color: #00FF00). self.wait(2.0).
Continue the clockwise sweep from the new pivot position without pause. self.wait(1.5).

sections.title: The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line
lecture_lines: Color points on each side of the line differently.
Pick a line splitting points into two equal sets.
As the line pivots, points swap sides across it.
The current pivot and the new pivot trade places.
The total count on each side remains perfectly balanced.
animations: Draw a balanced line through a pivot with 2 blue points (#0000FF) on the left and 2 red points (#FF0000) on the right. self.wait(2.0).
Use blue and red SurroundingRectangles to group the points on either side. self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line; show the current pivot moving to the other side as the new point becomes the pivot. self.wait(2.0).
Use Arrows to show the points effectively exchanging places relative to the line. self.wait(1.5).
Flash the blue and red groups to show the total counts (2 on each side) remain unchanged. self.wait(2.0).

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
lecture_lines: After a half-rotation, the line returns to its angle.
However, the line is now oriented in reverse.
Points originally on the left are now on the right.
Every point must cross the line to swap sides.
This proves the windmill hits every star eventually.
animations: Show the initial balanced line with labeled sides and colored points (#0000FF and #FF0000). self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line slowly 180 degrees using a 'smooth' rate function (color: #FFD700). self.wait(3.0).
Morph the side labels and point colors to show the sides have completely swapped. self.wait(2.0).
Highlight each point in sequence as the line passes through it during the rotation. self.wait(1.5).
Flash all points in green (#00FF00) to signify the proof is complete. self.wait(2.0).

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Local rules create a beautiful, predictable global cycle.
This visual logic solved the hardest IMO 2011 problem.
Simple rotations reveal deep truths in geometry and combinatorics.
animations: Show a fast-motion animation of a 10-point windmill completing a full cycle. self.wait(2.0).
Display the text 'IMO 2011 Problem 2' in gold (#FFD700). self.wait(1.5).
Fade out the points and line into a final geometric pattern. self.wait(2.0).
